body_builder_image_handling._question: any resize, crop or re-encode in OUR OWN body builder
body_builder_image_handling.answer: NONE. bodies.image_part (bodies.py:131-147) puts the stored file's bytes on the wire base64-encoded verbatim via _data_url (bodies.py:127-128), or a uuid-only reference when the device already uploaded them; materialize (bodies.py:150-170) only fills a deferred part with that same URL. No PIL import, no size argument, no crop, no re-encode anywhere in the module.
body_builder_image_handling.per_request_mm_processor_kwargs: NONE. build_body (bodies.py:211-240) assembles model, stream, messages, cache_salt, gen, optional kv_transfer_params and the fm_* / _live2 hint fields; it never sets mm_processor_kwargs, so --trust-request-mm-kwargs on the server has nothing to trust and the server-wide setting is the only one
body_builder_image_handling.the_only_re_encode_is_offline: data/encode_jpeg.py, PNG or CHW array -> JPEG q90 (Nexar) / q88 (S-EMBER), explicitly 'NO resize in the encode step' (encode_jpeg.py:262) and asserting the expected pixel grid before writing (lines 103-107, 118-120)
body_builder_image_handling.frames_root: the coordinator resolves frames_root / frame_ref and sends nothing if the file is absent (coordinator.py:1327-1335); a real-server run is REFUSED if any ref has no file (preflight.require_frames), and the committed frames_preflight.json of every cell used here reports n_missing 0, so every image on the wire carried real bytes

assistance_vs_the_others._question: are ASSISTANCE images capped by the same rule as the other two types
assistance_vs_the_others.answer: SAME RULE, and the rule binds nothing. There is exactly one image-processor setting, server-wide, for all three types: min_pixels 4096 and max_pixels 16777216. The largest image any type sends is 1,786,368 px, 9.4x below max_pixels, and the smallest is 196,608 px, 48x above min_pixels, so no image of any type is rescaled by the processor.
assistance_vs_the_others.what_actually_differs: the SOURCE pixel grid, not the cap. Alert and recall frames were downsized OFFLINE to a fixed grid before storage (Nexar SMALL 768x432, S-EMBER D2 352x256); assistance images are stored and sent at the dataset's NATIVE resolution with no pre-resize step anywhere in the pipeline.

single_shot_assistance.device: Orin 4B, vLLM 0.20.0, orin3_serve.sh:16 passes --limit-mm-per-prompt only and NO --mm-processor-kwargs, so the released Qwen3-VL-4B defaults apply: size {shortest_edge 65536, longest_edge 16777216}, patch 16, merge 2 (reports/study_ss2.md:110-113)
single_shot_assistance.match: PARTIAL BY FLAG, EXACT IN EFFECT. max_pixels is identical; only the min_pixels floor differs (65536 against 4096) and it binds on no SS2 image, the smallest being 196,608 px, 3.0x the device floor. StudySS2 checked this as a census and found prompt-token counts identical on 1,042 of 1,042 questions (reports/study_ss2.md:279-294).

alert_dashcam.device: Orin 4B, sh_ep_server_orin.sh:43 passes the SAME --mm-processor-kwargs string as the H100 (lines 19-20 state the parity requirement explicitly)
alert_dashcam.match: YES, byte for byte. --limit-mm-per-prompt differs (image 21 on the Orin against image 640 on the H100) but that is an admission limit, not a pixel budget, and EP-G is capped at 21 frames.

device_measurement_comparison.cost_tables: reports/phase1_cost_profiling.md and results/cost/cost_matrix.csv are TEXT-token representation costs (full / window / summary) with no image input; they carry no image-processor setting and none is needed.

finding_settings_differ_without_a_record.the_difference: alert frames reach the store already downsized to 768x432 (338 tokens) and recall frames to 352x256 (90 tokens), while assistance images are sent at native resolution, p50 1152x938 and up to 1536x1536, for a p50 of 1,307 image tokens: 3.9x an alert frame and 14.5x a recall frame. The image-processor SETTING is one and the same for all three; the effective per-image token cost is not.
finding_settings_differ_without_a_record.what_the_d_rows_do_cover: D70 and D91 fix the WIRE FORMAT (JPEG) and the stored grids for Nexar and S-EMBER, whose sizes come from the upstream studies (StudyD14 SMALL; study_rh3_inputs.load (352, 256)), not from a live2 sizing decision. D136 and D143 choose the SS datasets and the split and say nothing about image size. D172 requires only that the settings be STATED, which is what this file does.
finding_settings_differ_without_a_record.status: DIFFERENCE WITHOUT A RECORDED DECISION. It is a finding to report, not a defect to fix here; whether to equalise the grids is a methodological change and the user's to rule on.

why_assistance_is_larger_than_alert._question: does image size explain assistance's 1,372 uncached tokens against alert's 374
why_assistance_is_larger_than_alert.answer: PARTLY, AND IT IS THE PART THAT DECIDES OVERSIZE. Two causes compound and the decomposition separates them.

cause_1_residency.effect: alert's EP-G episode is append-only, so a typical alert request is charged about ONE new frame on a warm prefix; assistance holds ZERO residency by construction (trace.py:567-574), so it is charged its whole prompt every time. This alone takes alert from a 3,760-token prompt to 374 uncached.

counterfactual_assistance_on_the_alert_g._construction: a CONSTRUCTED bound, not a measurement: each assistance request's measured text residual plus 338, i.e. what it would cost if its image came to the store downsized to 768x432 as a Nexar frame does
counterfactual_assistance_on_the_alert_g.reading: at the native grid the median assistance request is 1.63x its own share and takes an OVERSIZE branch; on the alert grid it would be about 0.48x its share and inside it. So the type's oversize status turns on the image grid, which no D-row sets, and not on the admission rule.

why_assistance_is_larger_than_alert._do_not_read_this_as: a claim that equalising the grids would improve any policy result. It would change the workload, which is a methodological change.

proxies_declared.valid_for_the_claim: NO, and the code says so: SS2 areas are 2.2x to 24x larger, so the substitution almost certainly UNDERSTATES assistive uplink. It does not touch token counts and so does not affect this file.
